findings.source_passage: So strongly and metaphysically did I conceive of my situation then, that while earnestly watching his motions, I seemed distinctly to perceive that my own individuality was now merged in a joint stock company of two
findings.why_it_matters: This is one of the most critically engaged passages in the chapter—the exact phrasing 'joint stock company of two' and 'my free will had received a mortal wound' are philosophically loaded formulations the critical tradition treats as signature. The draft reduces 'joint-stock of two' (dropping 'company') and drops 'received a mortal wound' in its exact form.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore verbatim: 'my own individuality was now merged in a joint stock company of two; that my free will had received a mortal wound.'

findings.source_passage: I saw that here was a sort of interregnum in Providence; for its even-handed equity never could have so gross an injustice.
findings.why_it_matters: The clause 'for its even-handed equity never could have so gross an injustice' is the interpretive crux of the Providence argument—it names the theological problem directly. The draft merely says 'Here, I thought, was an interregnum in Providence,' silently dropping the equity-and-injustice reasoning that makes the passage philosophically weighty.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore: 'for its even-handed equity never could have so gross an injustice' immediately after naming the interregnum.

findings.source_passage: only, in most cases, he, one way or other, has this Siamese connexion with a plurality of other mortals
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'So strongly and metaphysically', after the Providence sentence
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'Siamese connexion' is the rhetorically distinctive term Melville plants here to yoke the personal incident to universal human interdependence; the draft substitutes 'tied … to a plurality of others,' losing the Siamese ligature motif that governs the whole chapter.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'this Siamese connexion with a plurality of other mortals' verbatim or very close to verbatim.

findings.source_passage: Are you not the precious image of each and all of us men in this whaling world? That unsounded ocean you gasp in, is Life; those sharks, your foes; those spades, your friends
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Well, well, my dear comrade'
findings.why_it_matters: The draft converts the rhetorical question into a statement ('is not this the image…') and truncates the apostrophe, losing the second-person direct address ('you gasp in') that gives the passage its lyric intensity and makes it a recognizable set-piece.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the rhetorical question form and include 'That unsounded ocean you gasp in, is Life' with Ishmael addressing Queequeg directly, including the full concluding phrase 'poor lad.'

findings.source_passage: But courage! there is good cheer in store for you, Queequeg. For now, as with blue lips and blood-shot eyes the exhausted savage at last climbs up the chains
findings.why_it_matters: The exclamatory 'But courage! there is good cheer in store for you, Queequeg' is a tonal pivot—mock-heroic and warmly ironic—that the draft collapses into 'But courage—good cheer came when,' stripping the direct address and the build-up that makes the ginger-water anti-climax land.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'But courage! there is good cheer in store for you, Queequeg' as a full exclamatory sentence before the scene.

findings.source_passage: Ginger! is ginger the sort of fuel you use, Dough-boy, to kindle a fire in this shivering cannibal? Ginger!—what the devil is ginger? Sea-coal? firewood?—lucifer matches?—tinder?—gunpowder?—what the devil is ginger, I say, that you offer this cup to our poor Queequeg here.
findings.source_locator: Stubb's speech beginning 'Ginger? ginger? and will you have the goodness'
findings.why_it_matters: The rhetorical catalogue—'Sea-coal? firewood?—lucifer matches?—tinder?—gunpowder?'—is rhythmically and comically distinctive; the draft compresses it adequately in list form but omits 'what the devil is ginger, I say, that you offer this cup to our poor Queequeg here,' which is the payoff line closing the rant.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the closing line of Stubb's harangue: 'what the devil is ginger, I say, that you offer this cup to our poor Queequeg here.'

findings.source_passage: You have seen Italian organ-boys holding a dancing-ape by a long cord. Just so, from the ship's steep side, did I hold Queequeg
findings.why_it_matters: The organ-boy simile is a lively image-signature that makes the monkey-rope setup vivid and whimsical; its absence slightly flattens the introduction of the device.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert the organ-boy simile: 'You have seen Italian organ-boys holding a dancing-ape by a long cord—just so did I hold Queequeg from the ship's steep side.'

summary: The draft loses or fatally flattens three high-severity signature passages (the 'joint stock company' / 'mortal wound' formulation, the Providence equity clause, and the 'Siamese connexion' wording) plus several medium-severity voice passages, requiring regeneration.
